label: Berge-Thierry et al. (2003)
units: SA in g at the API boundary; the model's own units and log base are kept under parameters
validityScope: Single-site intensity only; no spatial correlation, so never use it to draw a correlated field across multiple assets. Valid only inside its own published magnitude, distance, period and damping envelope, recorded under parameters; outside it the wrapper refuses unless the caller sets allow_extrapolation. Not usable at version 0.1.0: coefficients are original_table_required - the catalogue gives the equation and metadata only, with no numerical coefficients - so construction raises CoefficientsUnavailable and no capability is declared. What is missing is named under parameters.coefficients.needed.

source.catalogue: Douglas, J. (2011). Ground-motion prediction equations 1964-2010. PEER Report 2011/102 / BRGM/RP-59356-FR.
source.benchmark_spec: gmpe_30_coding_prompts.md, sections 3 and 4 - the 30-family benchmark set definition.
source.caveat: Douglas (2011) is a catalogue, not a ranking, and warns that a report of its size may contain errors or omissions. Every envelope below is its summary, frequently approximate. Nothing here substitutes for the original publication.
source.coefficient_appendix: gmpe_30_coding_prompts_with_coefficients.md sections 11 and 12 - coefficients transcribed from Douglas (2011), with an explicit per-model completeness status and a coefficient-completeness gate.

parameters.label: Berge-Thierry et al. (2003)

magnitude.note: Ms. The 163 W. USA records enter on Mw, treated by the authors as equivalent to Ms above Mw 6. Do not feed Mw.

site.anchor_note: c1(f) applies to rock (Vs30 > 800 m/s) and c2(f) to alluvium (300 < Vs30 < 800 m/s).

mechanism.note: No mechanism term in the form Douglas summarises.

parameters.equation: log10 PSA(f) = a(f)*M + b(f)*d - log10(d) + c1(f) + c2(f)

coefficients.needed: The frequency-dependent a(f), b(f), c1(f) and c2(f) for all four damping ratios. The appendix reproduces the functional form and site terms only, explicitly NOT_REPRODUCED_IN_DOUGLAS.

implementation_notes: Support only 5, 7, 10 and 20% damping unless the source gives an interpolation rule.
The log10 convention is explicit here - preserve it.

resolution_provenance.magnitude.scale: Douglas (2011) BRGM/RP-59356-FR, Illustration 2 (spectral characteristics table): 'Ms (Mw for W. USA)'; Douglas (2011) BRGM/RP-59356-FR, section 4.109: uniformly calculated Ms for the European data and Mw for the W. USA records, which the authors treat as equivalent to Ms for Mw > 6.
resolution_provenance.distance.min_km: Douglas (2011) BRGM/RP-59356-FR, Illustration 2 (spectral characteristics table): rmin 4 km (rhypo)
resolution_provenance.distance.max_km: Douglas (2011) BRGM/RP-59356-FR, Illustration 2 (spectral characteristics table): rmax 330 km (rhypo)
resolution_provenance.component: Douglas (2011) BRGM/RP-59356-FR, Illustration 2 (spectral characteristics table): component code B (each horizontal as a separate observation); OpenQuake hazardlib (gem/oq-engine master, retrieved 2026-10-04), openquake/hazardlib/gsim/berge_thierry_2003.py declares IMC.HORIZONTAL (p. 196)
resolution_provenance.internal_units: OpenQuake hazardlib (gem/oq-engine master, retrieved 2026-10-04), openquake/hazardlib/gsim/berge_thierry_2003.py: 'convert from log10 to ln, and from cm/s2 to g'. External implementation; Douglas does not state units.
resolution_provenance.periods.grid: OpenQuake hazardlib (gem/oq-engine master, retrieved 2026-10-04), openquake/hazardlib/gsim/berge_thierry_2003.py coefficient table; period count and range (143 periods, 0.03-10 s) match Douglas (2011) BRGM/RP-59356-FR, Illustration 2 (spectral characteristics table). External implementation, original paper not checked. Periods are reciprocals of the published frequencies, hence the odd values (0.029412 s = 34 Hz). Douglas footnote: 'On page 8 of paper it says 88 periods' -- the 143 count is the table's, check the paper before relying on either.
